triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: this Mitya, or rather Dmitri Fyodorovitch, was the only one of Fyodor Pavlovitch’s three sons who grew up in the belief that he had property

triples.subject: Grigory
triples.quote: a faithful servant of the family, Grigory, took the three-year-old Mitya into his care.

triples.subject: Grigory
triples.quote: a faithful servant of the family, Grigory, took the three-year-old Mitya into his care.

triples.subject: Pyotr Alexandrovitch Miüsov
triples.quote: a cousin of Mitya’s mother, Pyotr Alexandrovitch Miüsov, happened to return from Paris.

triples.subject: Pyotr Alexandrovitch Miüsov
triples.quote: Mitya did, in fact, pass into this cousin’s keeping, but as the latter had no family of his own

triples.subject: Pyotr Alexandrovitch Miüsov
triples.quote: settling permanently in Paris he, too, forgot the child, especially when the Revolution of February broke out

triples.subject: Pyotr Alexandrovitch Miüsov
triples.quote: describing the three days of the Paris Revolution of February 1848, hinting that he himself had almost taken part in the fighting on the barricades.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: he had received the whole value of his property in sums of money from Fyodor Pavlovitch, and was perhaps even in debt to him

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: He seems not to have liked his father. He did not stay long with him, and made haste to get away
